-- Free rule filters: run before the AI so obvious rejects cost nothing.
WITH f AS (
  SELECT id,
    CASE
      WHEN title ~* '\m(senior|sr|lead|principal|staff|manager|head|director|gerente|jefe|l[ií]der)\M'
        THEN 'Seniority in title'
      WHEN title !~* '(data|datos|analyst|analista|\mbi\M|business intelligence|reporting|insights)'
        THEN 'Off-target title'
      WHEN upper(coalesce(salary_currency, '')) = 'COP' AND salary_max IS NOT NULL
           AND (CASE upper(coalesce(salary_period, ''))
                  WHEN 'YEAR'  THEN salary_max / 12
                  WHEN 'MONTH' THEN salary_max
                END) < 2500000
        THEN 'Salary below 2,500,000 COP/month'
      WHEN NOT (
             work_mode = 'remote'
          OR coalesce(location, '') ~* '(medell|antioquia|envigado|itag|sabaneta|\mbello\M|rionegro)'
          OR coalesce(location, '') ~* '^\s*colombia\s*$'
          OR coalesce(location, '') ~* '(remote|remoto|anywhere|latam|latin america)'
        )
        THEN 'Not remote and outside Medellín'
    END AS reason
  FROM jobs
  WHERE status = 'found'
),
upd AS (
  UPDATE jobs j
  SET status = 'filtered_out', filter_reason = f.reason
  FROM f
  WHERE j.id = f.id AND f.reason IS NOT NULL
  RETURNING j.id
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM upd) AS filtered_out,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM f WHERE reason IS NULL) AS to_score;

SELECT id, title, company, location, work_mode, description,
       salary_min, salary_max, salary_currency, salary_period
FROM jobs
WHERE status = 'found'
ORDER BY found_at DESC
LIMIT 25;

WITH s AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS x(
    id bigint, score int, matched_skills jsonb, missing_skills jsonb, red_flags jsonb,
    reasoning text, disqualify_reason text, job_language text, confidence text
  )
)
UPDATE jobs j
SET status           = CASE WHEN s.disqualify_reason IS NOT NULL THEN 'filtered_out' ELSE 'scored' END,
    filter_reason    = CASE WHEN s.disqualify_reason IS NOT NULL THEN 'AI: ' || s.disqualify_reason ELSE j.filter_reason END,
    match_score      = s.score,
    matched_skills   = ARRAY(SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text(s.matched_skills)),
    missing_skills   = ARRAY(SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text(s.missing_skills)),
    red_flags        = ARRAY(SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text(s.red_flags)),
    match_reasoning  = s.reasoning,
    language         = s.job_language,
    score_confidence = s.confidence
FROM s
WHERE j.id = s.id AND j.status = 'found'
RETURNING j.id, j.title, j.company, j.status, j.match_score;

-- LinkedIn jobs scored from title only that look promising: look up their description.
-- Max 2 per day = ~60 JSearch requests/month.
SELECT id, title, company
FROM jobs
WHERE source = 'linkedin_alert'
  AND status = 'scored'
  AND score_confidence = 'title_only'
  AND match_score >= 60
  AND NOT enrich_attempted
ORDER BY match_score DESC
LIMIT 2;

WITH s AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS x(
    id bigint, description text, salary_min numeric, salary_max numeric,
    salary_currency text, salary_period text
  )
)
UPDATE jobs j
SET enrich_attempted = true,
    description      = coalesce(s.description, j.description),
    salary_min       = coalesce(s.salary_min, j.salary_min),
    salary_max       = coalesce(s.salary_max, j.salary_max),
    salary_currency  = coalesce(s.salary_currency, j.salary_currency),
    salary_period    = coalesce(s.salary_period, j.salary_period),
    -- back to 'found' so the next scoring run re-scores it with the full description
    status           = CASE WHEN s.description IS NOT NULL THEN 'found' ELSE j.status END
FROM s
WHERE j.id = s.id
RETURNING j.id, j.title, j.status;
